sentences.text:
Rajendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 July, 2018
 Cr.R. No.3081/2018 1
 Rajendra S/o Babulal vs. State of M.P.
 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
Indore : 18/07/2018 :-
 Shri Ashish Jaiswal, learned counsel for the petitioner.
 Shri Hemant Sharma, learned Government Advocate for
the respondent/State.

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard on the question of admission.
Appeal is admitted for final hearing.

Also heard on IA No.5030/2018, an application for suspension of sentence under Section 389 (1) of Cr.P.C.
Appellant is convicted for the offence punishable under Section 16 (I) (A) (I) (II) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced to undergo six months RI with fine of Rs.1,000/- with default stipulation by the JMFC, Thandla, District-Jhabua in criminal case No.804/2011 vide judgment dated 06/10/2017, which has been affirmed by I ASJ, Jhabua in criminal appeal No.186/2017 vide judgment dated 27/06/2018.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner has held guilty in contravention of Rule 32-E of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 which has been declared ultra virus by Hon'ble the Supreme Court of India in Dwarka Nath and another vs. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi reported in 1972 FAC 1 (SC), NCT of Delhi vs. Mohinder Singh reported in 2016 (1) FAC 40 and Naresh Narubha Rathod vs. State of Gujarat and another reported in 2017 (2) FAC 464. Madhya Pradesh High Court has also followed the same field in Hariram vs. State of M.P. 2004 Rajendra S/o Babulal vs. State of M.P. (3) MPWN 23 and Ravindra Singh and another vs. State of M.P. and another reported in 2007 FAJ 455.
Second contention of the petitioner is that the incident took place on 29/07/2011, while the Old Act was repealed by the New Act on 29/07/2010, therefore, his prosecution under repealed Act is bad in law.

sentences.text: Prayer is opposed by learned Public Prosecutor.
Considering both the arguments and grounds for conviction and evidence produced by the prosecution, I am of the opinion that petitioner has made out a case for suspension of jail sentence.
Thus, the application (IA No.5030/2018) for suspension of sentence is allowed.

It is directed that on deposition of fine amount and also on furnishing personal bond of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before this Court/Registry on 06/03/2019 and on all other subsequent dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this behalf

, the execution of substantial jail sentence imposed on the petitioner shall remain suspended, till the final Rajendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78799772/
1 disposal of this revision.
A copy of this order be sent to Court concerned for it's compliance.
Let the matter be fixed for final hearing in due course.
(Virender Singh) Judge Aiyer*
